newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul Fin Min denies report on foreign stock limit.
newsitem.headline: Seoul Fin Min denies report on foreign stock limit.

text.p: South Korea's finance ministry on Tuesday denied media reports that the ministry planned to raise the foreign stock ownership limit further to 25 to 26 percent this year from the current 23 percent.

On Monday, Yonhap Television News said the limit would be expanded further to 30 percent in 1998 and 35 percent in 1999 before complete liberalisation in 2000, quoting a finance ministry report to the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD).
"It is not true the finance ministry has sent such a revised report to the OECD," said Kim Woo-suk, director-general of the ministry's international finance and securities division.
Kim said the limit would be raised to 26 percent in 1998 and 29 percent in 1999 before being scrapped in 2000 according to the ministry's plans submitted to the OECD last year.
South Korea joined the club of rich nations in December last year, commiting itself to wider market opening.
"The foreign stock ownership limit could be raised faster than our original schedule depending on conditions in the stock and foreign exchange markets," Kim said.
Last week, the ministry denied similar newspaper reports that another increase in the ceiling was scheduled this year.
The ministry raised the ceiling to 23 percent on May 2 from 20 percent. The ceiling was raised twice last year.
